- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If model forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >5% gap) and sentiment is neutral or positive, consider mean reversion bias — adjust forecast toward recent mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true trend by 1–3 days; add 1–2% lagged momentum to forecast if sentiment is trending.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model fails to catch momentum; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% at flip point.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — sentiment history matters more than daily sentiment alone.
